purpose: Rebuild adoption/sdk/requirements-linux-x86_64-py313.lock in a brand-new isolated uv prefix with hash checking, then run the identity-provenance overturn_protocol's named baseline regression suite (tests.test_nanosecond_replay, tests.test_point_in_time), to establish the required zero-failure/zero-skip precondition that every overturn_protocol arm (DVC, DVC+OpenLineage, PyIceberg, ArcticDB) depends on.
preregistered: Expected result if the project hash-manifest baseline is intact: `uv pip install --require-hashes` installs all 36 locked distributions with no hash mismatch in a prefix that did not previously exist, and `python3 -m unittest tests.test_nanosecond_replay tests.test_point_in_time -v` reports 0 failures and 0 skips. Any hash mismatch, install failure, test failure, or skip would mean the overturn_protocol's required precondition is not met and no arm comparison (including dvc-arm-restore-compare) could be trusted.

verdict_impact.explanation: Establishes the zero-failure/zero-skip baseline precondition the overturn_protocol requires before any arm (DVC, DVC+OpenLineage, PyIceberg, ArcticDB) can be meaningfully compared. This alone does not run any arm; see dvc-arm-restore-compare for the DVC arm result. PyIceberg and ArcticDB arms were not attempted (out of scope for this unit's 5 assigned checks) and remain open.

limitations: Only the DVC arm was executed as part of this unit's assigned checks (see dvc-arm-restore-compare.json); PyIceberg and ArcticDB arms from the overturn_protocol were not run.
This confirms hash-lock reproducibility and baseline correctness, not licensed market-data entitlement or a real historical universe (gap 4/5, both needs_paid_entitlement and out of scope here).

The `preregistered` field above was written after these commands had already been run and their results (36/36 installs, 25/25 tests, 0 failures/skips) were known, so it is a post-hoc restatement of the expected outcome rather than a true blind prediction recorded before execution.
